title: Readers — the value of pkit::documentation:readers, version 1
description: The data point's companion schema (COR-052 point 5; living-docs DEC-001 point 7): who reads the documentation, what they need and the paths they take. The point is `union`: entries from every filler merge by `id`, a project entry replacing a capability's or the default's whole, and the project may drop one under `remove` with a reason. The default — `user` and `maintainer`, one per mandatory space — always takes part, so a project has readers on day one; a capability that keeps knowledge about the software's users may add its own, under ids of its own. A page names one of these ids as its `reader` (schemas/page.schema.json). Where RS-LDOC-003 binds on the page, the capability's validator fails it when its reader does not resolve. The inert policy is `fail`: a filler that cannot answer leaves the whole point unresolved, and no page's reader is checked until it does. The version rises only on a change that breaks existing fillers.

word.description: A lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: the shape a page's `reader` field takes.

id.description: The reader's id, which a page names as its `reader`. Distinct from the ids an analysis capability gives its actors (DEC-001 point 7).

description.description: Who the reader is and what they need from the documentation — what a reader-review reads a page against (DEC-001 point 6).

paths.description: The paths the reader takes through the pages (DEC-001 point 7). A reader-review takes them with the reader, and follows those through the page it reads where a rule asks that reader paths stay unbroken, as the user space's own rule does (DEC-001 points 3 and 6). Optional: the default's readers carry none, since only the project knows its pages. No check reads them: whether a path's pages exist and link on to one another is the reader-review's to judge.

path.description: One path a reader takes: the pages they read, in order, from the page they start at. The path is unbroken where each page links on to the next.

description.description: What the reader comes to do along the path.

pages.description: The pages the reader reads, in order, the first where they start.

page.description: A page, named by the path of its Markdown file from the repository's root, folders joined by `/`: no leading `/`, no `.` or `..` folder, no glob character, and no `#` section. A path names pages, never a pattern of files.
